text:
jules: FYI opened a PR to fix the generate response usage fields. Docs currently show top-level `tokens` array in examples but the API returns `usage.token_count` (and SDKs are inconsistent). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1289

kevin: Which SDK is returning what?

jules: Quick summary from integration tests:
- Python SDK: historically surfaced `token_count` as a top-level field (legacy shim).
- Go SDK: usage.TotalTokens in the typed struct.
- JS SDK: usage.totalTokens (camelCase).

rania: Oof. That's going to confuse customers and our examples. I think canonical shape should be `usage` object with snake_case fields (usage.total_tokens, usage.prompt_tokens, usage.completion_tokens) in the docs/OpenAPI and SDKs should map aliases.

kevin: Agreed on canonical. Backend already emits a `usage` object in telemetry. We just need docs and SDK codegen alignment.

jules: Plan in the PR: update OpenAPI response schema for /v1/generate to define components/schemas/Usage with snake_case names and mark `token_count` (top-level) as deprecated with a short migration note. Add examples for curl/python/go that show the new shape.

rania: Can we also add a small compatibility paragraph: "If your integration reads top-level `token_count`, please switch to `usage.total_tokens` — SDKs will accept either for one release and then drop the top-level alias in the next major."

docs-bot: Deploy preview: https://deploy-preview.docs.redwood.ai/1289  examples updated.

kevin: Will codegen pick up `x-sdk-alias` automatically? We should add that property to the OpenAPI schema fields so generated clients keep previous names for one release.

jules: Yes adding `x-sdk-alias` to each usage field (e.g., total_tokens -> totalTokens/TotalTokens/token_count depending on target). Also adding `deprecated: true` to the top-level `token_count` schema entry.

rania: One more: update the examples page that shows the streaming SSE payloads — right now the event `tokens` field in the SSE example is misleading. We'll change SSE snippets to include `usage` after completion or show incremental `partial_token_count` if we need streaming deltas.

kevin: Good call. For streaming, let's keep incremental events emitting `delta_tokens` and final event includes full `usage`. Add a short note in the SSE docs.

jules: Updated PR includes:
- OpenAPI components/schemas/Usage (snake_case)
- Deprecated top-level `token_count` with deprecation note
- x-sdk-alias entries for codegen compatibility
- Curl/JS/Python/Go examples swapped to new shape
- SSE example updated to show `delta_tokens` per chunk and final `usage` object

Example curl response snippet in docs (now):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "id": "gen_abc123",
  "output": "...",
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 32,
    "completion_tokens": 18,
    "total_tokens": 50
  }
}
```

Python example snippet (docs/SDK usage):
```
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-1", input="x")
print(resp.usage.total_tokens)  # 50
# older resp.token_count will still work during migration window
```

Go example (docs snippet):
```
resp, _ := client.Generate(ctx, opts)
fmt.Println(resp.Usage.TotalTokens)
```

kevin: Tests: I'll update the API integration tests to assert presence of `usage.total_tokens` and the deprecation header for `token_count`. rania, can you follow up on the examples page copy?

rania: On it. I'll also add a short migration FAQ entry under /docs/migration saying how long the shim lasts and example mapping.

jules: Reviewer checklist in PR description:
- [ ] Update OpenAPI schemas (done in branch)
- [ ] Add x-sdk-alias fields (done)
- [ ] Update examples across languages (done)
- [ ] Update SSE streaming docs (done)
- [ ] Run codegen and confirm SDK unit tests (in progress, kevin)
- [ ] Merge when CI green and SDKs validated

kevin: I'll kick codegen/jobs after CI passes. If anything breaks, we can revert examples quickly.

jules: Thanks folks. If anyone spots more mismatches on the generate or streaming docs ping here and I'll fold into the PR. :thumbsup:
__notes: Slack thread: brief cross-team coordination for docs PR standardizing usage/token fields in generate responses and streaming examples
